# Spec: confirm a row into its matched existing expense, and see that expense first

## Problem
On the bank-statement Review page (`/bank-statements/:id`), the "Process ready"
bulk action already links a row to an existing unlinked expense when the matcher
returns `AutoLink` (receipt-backed expenses now win that match). But the per-row
UI does not expose this:

1. A row that will auto-link shows a static `↔ Link existing` chip that is not
   clickable, and the row's Match and Category cells show the import-rule / AI
   *suggestion*, not the matched expense's own merchant/category. The user cannot
   see which expense will be linked or its real merchant/category/notes, which
   usually differ from the suggestion.
2. The per-row primary button "Confirm" always opens the create-expense drawer
   (`BankRowCreateExpenseForm`), which lists unconfirmed *receipts* only. So when a
   row matches an existing expense, there is no per-row way to confirm *that link*;
   the only path to link an existing expense is buried in the "…" menu.

Goal: let the user confirm a single row into its matched existing expense (keeping
the link, same outcome as the bulk action), after seeing that expense's details.
The bulk "Process ready" flow stays exactly as it is.

## Relevant files (all under `web/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/components/pages/bankstatementreview/`)
- `BankStatementReviewRow.scala` — one table row. `Props.linksToExpense: Boolean`
  (line ~47) is the collapsed match flag; the `↔ Link existing` chip is a static
  `tintChip` (~line 175); `primaryActionFor` drives the primary button, and
  `PrimaryAction.ReviewExpense` renders "Confirm" → `RowAction.OpenExpenseForm`
  (~line 96-103). `matchCell` (~162) and `categoryCell` (~184) render the
  suggestion for not-yet-linked rows.
- `BankStatementReviewTable.scala` (~line 87) builds `linksToExpense` from
  `props.expenseMatchById.get(row.id)`, discarding the `AutoLink(expenseId)` id.
- `BankStatementReviewContent.scala` (~line 150-152) maps `RowAction.OpenExpenseForm`
  → `DrawerState.CreateExpense(rowId)` and `RowAction.OpenLinkPicker` →
  `DrawerState.LinkExpense(rowId)`. It holds the loaded expenses, categories, and
  merchants and builds `expenseMatchById`.
- `BankRowLinkPicker.scala` — the existing "Link to existing expense" drawer: loads
  all expenses via `getExpenses`, filters, and renders `date | amount | merchant |
  notes` rows each with a "Link" button that calls `linkRowToExpense`. This is the
  working link path; reuse it.
- `BankStatementReviewLogic.scala` — `primaryActionFor` (~line 277), the
  `PrimaryAction` enum (~274), `RowInfo`. `ReconciliationMatcher.AutoLink(expenseId)`
  carries the matched expense id.
- `BankStatementRowActions.scala` — row-level API calls (`unlink`, `refreshRow`, …);
  `BankStatementReviewContent` already calls `linkRowToExpense` indirectly via the
  picker's `onSuccess`.

## Required behavior

### Thread the matched expense through to the row
Stop collapsing the match to a `Boolean`. Pass the matched expense id (from
`ReconciliationMatcher.AutoLink(expenseId)`) down to `BankStatementReviewRow`, and
resolve it to the already-loaded expense so the row can show its real data. Prefer
computing a small prepared value in the page/parent (matched expense id + its
merchant name + a category label built from its splits and the loaded categories,
"Multiple" when the splits span more than one category) and passing that to the
row, keeping the row component dumb. Do not add a new API call for this; the
expenses, categories and merchants are already loaded on the page.

### Gap 1 — show and inspect the matched expense
- When a not-yet-linked row has an `AutoLink` match, the Match cell shows the
  matched expense's merchant and the Category cell shows the matched expense's
  category label (not the rule/AI suggestion). Keep the `↔ Link existing` chip.
- Make the match affordance clickable: clicking it opens the link drawer for that
  row (see below) so the user can see the full expense (merchant, category, notes,
  amount, date, whether it has a receipt) before deciding. A static, unclickable
  chip is the current bug.

### Gap 2 — per-row "Confirm" links the matched expense
- When a row is ready (`PrimaryAction.ReviewExpense`) AND has an `AutoLink` match,
  "Confirm" opens the link drawer (`DrawerState.LinkExpense(rowId)`) instead of the
  create-expense drawer. Linking keeps the row linked to that existing expense
  (reuse `linkRowToExpense`), which inherits the expense's merchant/category/notes.
- When a ready row has no match, "Confirm" keeps opening the create-expense drawer
  as today.
- Keep the "…" menu entries ("Link to existing expense", "Create expense", etc.)
  as manual overrides, so the user can still create a new expense or pick a
  different one.

### Enhance `BankRowLinkPicker` to surface the match
- Accept an optional matched/suggested expense id. When present, show that expense
  first and prominently, with its full details: merchant, category (resolved from
  splits + categories, "Multiple" if several), notes, amount, date, and a receipt
  indicator if it has one. Give it a primary "Link this expense" button.
- Keep the existing filter and full list below as manual override, and make sure
  the matched expense is always shown even if it would fall outside the current
  `take(20)` slice.
- To render category names the picker needs the categories; pass them in from the
  page (already loaded) rather than fetching.

## Acceptance tests
Favor extracting pure logic into `BankStatementReviewLogic` and unit-testing it in
`BankStatementReviewLogicSpec`; add a thin component test only where it needs the
DOM.
1. `primaryActionFor` (or a new helper): a ready row with an `AutoLink` match
   resolves its "Confirm" to the link action; a ready row without a match resolves
   to the create action. Unignore / ignore-by-rule / refund cases unchanged.
2. The prepared-match helper: given an `AutoLink(expenseId)`, the loaded expenses,
   categories and merchants, it yields the matched expense's merchant name and the
   correct category label (single category name; "Multiple" for multi-split;
   empty/greyed when the expense or category is missing). A non-`AutoLink` match or
   a missing expense yields no prepared match.
3. Component test (BrowserRouter + jsdom, per docs/guide/testing.md): a row with a
   match renders the matched expense's merchant/category and a clickable `↔ Link
   existing`; clicking "Confirm" opens the link drawer (not the create drawer); the
   link drawer shows the matched expense first with a "Link this expense" button.
4. Existing bank-statement-review tests still pass unchanged, and bulk "Process
   ready" behavior is untouched.

## Repo conventions (must follow)
- Frontend only. No new API endpoints and no DB schema changes; reuse
  `linkRowToExpense`, `getExpenses`, and the loaded categories/merchants.
- Hook dependency lists go through `net.wiringbits.core.SafeHooks` with `String`
  keys (never a `UUID`, `Option`, collection or case class as a raw dep).
- Mutually-exclusive UI state is one ADT in a single `useState`, not parallel
  flags; derive state from its previous value with the functional updater
  (`set(_ + x)`), never `set(closureValue + x)`.
- Component tests use `BrowserRouter` + jsdom; `null.asInstanceOf[API]` only when
  the component never calls `ctx.api`; object-level `val`s hold only plain JS
  literals; React elements reused in a render tree use `def`, not `val`.
- Comments explain intent, not the change history.
- Pre-push sequence, in this exact order:
  1. `CI=true sbt Test/compile`
  2. `git add` new/changed files
  3. `sbt scalafmtAll scalafmtSbt`, then re-stage reformatted files
  4. `CI=true NODE_OPTIONS=--openssl-legacy-provider sbt test` (foreground) must exit 0
  5. push
- The repo is public: keep commit messages and the PR description free of any PII
  (account numbers, real merchant names, amounts) and free of Claude session links.
- Surgical changes, match existing style, keep the bulk flow and the server
  untouched.
